rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Specific heat is not latent heat. Latent heat changes the state at constant temperature.  ·  c and C are different. C = mc.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The container's mc must be included if the question gives it.  ·  A negative Q means heat left the body.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Specific heat capacity c is the heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 K. The defining relation is Q = mc Δθ, so c = Q / (m Δθ).  ·  The SI unit is joule per kilogram per kelvin, J kg^-1 K^-1. A degree Celsius interval equals a kelvin interval, so J kg^-1 °C^-1 is the same size of unit.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: A temperature in °C may be used for a difference. A formula that needs the thermodynamic temperature needs kelvin.  ·  The calorie is an older heat unit. The SI answer is in joules.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Heat Q has the dimensions of energy, [M L^2 T^-2]. Mass is [M] and a temperature interval brings in [K]. Therefore [c] = [L^2 T^-2 K^-1].  ·  Water's specific heat is about 4200 J kg^-1 K^-1, which is large. That is why a large mass of water changes temperature slowly for a given heat input.  ·  The heat capacity of a whole body is C = mc, in J/K. Specific heat is a material property. Heat capacity belongs to one particular object.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Dimensions follow from Q = mc Δθ.  ·  Specific Heat Capacity — Units & Dimensional Formula is based on fundamental principles.  ·  Name the substance, because c depends on it.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Do not use a latent-heat term when the temperature is changing inside one state.  ·  Water near 4200 J kg^-1 K^-1 is the comparison value.  ·  Write Q = mc Δθ and say what each symbol means.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.  ·  Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.  ·  Mixing problems use heat lost equals heat gained when the container is closed to outside heat. Each term is of the form mc Δθ, with the temperature change written as a positive quantity in that bookkeeping.
